uncited: Hard Voxelization converts a continuous 3D point cloud into a discrete, sparse voxel grid by assigning each point to a specific voxel cell based on its spatial coordinates and a fixed voxel size [S2, unofficial].
It differs from soft voxelization by using hard assignment (no interpolation) and from sparse voxel octrees by using a fixed-axis-aligned grid structure [S2, unofficial].
This method serves as the foundational step for producing volume data from raw point clouds, building on [Point Cloud Voxelization](1000-point-cloud-voxelization.md).

All variants in this family share the core mechanism of mapping continuous point coordinates $(x, y, z)$ to discrete integer voxel indices $(i, j, k)$ using floor division relative to a bounding box origin and voxel dimensions.
- **Definition**: Computes only the voxel coordinates for each point, without assigning points to a fixed voxel grid structure or handling duplicates/max points.

The deterministic variant was developed to address reproducibility issues in non-deterministic CUDA implementations where atomic operations could lead to race conditions and varying outputs across runs [S2, unofficial].
